The paper uses data from a 2.2 MW variable-speed, variable-pitch horizontal axis wind turbine.
The measured signals used for training the models include flap bending moments, edge bending moments, rotor speed, wind speed, and grid power.
The time window for the dynamic PCA (dPCA) model is set to 10 seconds, corresponding to 100 data points.
The number of principal components retained in the PCA model is chosen to explain 90% of the cumulative variance in the data, ranging from 4 to 8 components across the 4 operating regions.
The Autoencoder model uses a combination of convolutional and LSTM layers to capture the non-linear and time-varying dynamics of the wind turbine data.
The Autoencoder model is trained to minimize the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) between the original and reconstructed measurements.
The Generalized Likelihood Ratio (GLR) test is used to enhance the signal separation between healthy and faulty cases, compared to direct thresholding.
The threshold values for the fault detection statistics (SPE and MAE) are computed to achieve a 1% probability of false alarms.
Both the PCA and Autoencoder models achieve detection rates close to 100% for faults related to the flap bending moment sensor.
The Autoencoder model outperforms the PCA model in detecting faults related to the edge bending moment sensor.
The statistical evaluation shows the Autoencoder generally has higher detection rates, with some exceptions during the transient phase of certain fault scenarios.
The PCA model requires separate models for each operating region, while the Autoencoder can learn a single global non-linear model covering all regions.
Real-life blade fault data is used to validate the proposed condition monitoring framework, in addition to simulated fault scenarios.
The paper focuses on developing a condition monitoring framework for detecting blade faults in wind turbines, which is an important but sparsely reported topic in the literature.
The proposed learning-based approach leverages both linear (PCA) and non-linear (Autoencoder) models to capture the complex dynamics of wind turbine systems.
